manifests.title: Power-family grid
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Describe -2x^4. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Even, all-real domain, both ends down, range (-∞,0].
manifests.learnerOutcome: Compare power functions f(x)=ax^p and explain how exponent and coefficient control domain, symmetry, end behavior, and growth.

manifests.title: Large-input comparison
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Classify the exponent, state domain and symmetry, determine end behavior, and compare growth over a stated input region. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Compare power functions f(x)=ax^p and explain how exponent and coefficient control domain, symmetry, end behavior, and growth.

manifests.title: Exponent classification tree
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is describing every power only as steeper or flatter. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Compare power functions f(x)=ax^p and explain how exponent and coefficient control domain, symmetry, end behavior, and growth.

manifests.title: Polynomial anatomy
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: For 7-2x^4+5x^2. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Standard form -2x^4+5x^2+7; degree 4; leading coefficient -2.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify degree, leading term, coefficients, and standard form, and explain why the leading term governs large-input behavior.

manifests.title: Leading-term ratio
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Write standard form, identify degree and leading coefficient, and compare the full polynomial with its leading term for large |x|. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify degree, leading term, coefficients, and standard form, and explain why the leading term governs large-input behavior.

manifests.title: Local versus long-range view
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is replacing the polynomial by its leading term near the origin. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify degree, leading term, coefficients, and standard form, and explain why the leading term governs large-input behavior.

manifests.title: Four end families
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Determine end behavior of -3x^5+x^2. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Left end rises and right end falls.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine polynomial end behavior from degree parity and leading coefficient and express it verbally, graphically, and with limit-style notation.

manifests.title: Factored degree inventory
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Identify total degree and leading sign, then state both left and right directions. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine polynomial end behavior from degree parity and leading coefficient and express it verbally, graphically, and with limit-style notation.

manifests.title: Plausible graph filter
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is stating only one end or reading behavior from the constant term. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine polynomial end behavior from degree parity and leading coefficient and express it verbally, graphically, and with limit-style notation.

manifests.title: Zero-factor-intercept triangle
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Zeros of x^3-4x. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: x=-2,0,2.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Connect polynomial zeros, linear factors, solutions, and x-intercepts, and distinguish exact from approximate zeros.

manifests.title: Exact versus approximate roots
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Factor when possible, solve each factor, and distinguish exact roots from numerical estimates. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Connect polynomial zeros, linear factors, solutions, and x-intercepts, and distinguish exact from approximate zeros.

manifests.title: Window caution
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is reporting an intercept point as a zero or treating a decimal as exact. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Connect polynomial zeros, linear factors, solutions, and x-intercepts, and distinguish exact from approximate zeros.

manifests.title: Multiplicity gallery
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Analyze (x+2)^2(x-1)^3. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: -2 touches; 1 crosses with flattening.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Relate the multiplicity of a zero to sign changes, crossing or touching behavior, and local flattening.

manifests.title: Factor sign table
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Odd multiplicity crosses and changes sign; even multiplicity touches and preserves sign; larger multiplicity flattens. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Relate the multiplicity of a zero to sign changes, crossing or touching behavior, and local flattening.

manifests.title: Degree accounting
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is assuming every intercept is a simple crossing. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Relate the multiplicity of a zero to sign changes, crossing or touching behavior, and local flattening.

manifests.title: Polynomial graphing workflow
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Sketch (x+2)(x-1)^2. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Left down, right up; cross at -2, touch at 1; y-intercept 2.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct a polynomial graph from degree, leading coefficient, zeros, multiplicities, sign intervals, and selected points.

manifests.title: Aligned sign chart
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Determine end behavior, mark zeros and crossing type, test interval signs, compute the y-intercept, and connect smoothly. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct a polynomial graph from degree, leading coefficient, zeros, multiplicities, sign intervals, and selected points.

manifests.title: Valid versus impossible sketch
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is adding decorative wiggles unsupported by the algebra. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct a polynomial graph from degree, leading coefficient, zeros, multiplicities, sign intervals, and selected points.

manifests.title: Turning-point gallery
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Can degree 4 have five turns? Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: No; maximum 3.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use degree bounds, graph evidence, and function values to analyze turning points and extrema.

manifests.title: Local versus absolute extrema
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Use the degree-n maximum of n-1 turns and compare local extrema with end behavior to identify absolute extrema. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use degree bounds, graph evidence, and function values to analyze turning points and extrema.

manifests.title: Turn versus intercept
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is confusing an x-intercept with a turning point. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use degree bounds, graph evidence, and function values to analyze turning points and extrema.

manifests.title: Continuity crossing
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: For x^3-x-1 on (1,2). Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: P(1)=-1 and P(2)=5, so a root lies in (1,2).
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use polynomial continuity and sign changes to guarantee roots and bracket them within intervals.

manifests.title: Bisection tree
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Find opposite endpoint signs, conclude a zero exists, and refine the bracket by midpoint testing. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use polynomial continuity and sign changes to guarantee roots and bracket them within intervals.

manifests.title: Same-sign counterexamples
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is treating a sign-change interval as proof of exactly one root. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use polynomial continuity and sign changes to guarantee roots and bracket them within intervals.

manifests.title: Long-division layout
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Divide x^3+2x^2-5x-6 by x+3. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Quotient x^2-x-2, remainder 0.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Divide polynomials using long and synthetic division and verify the division algorithm P=DQ+R.

manifests.title: Synthetic correspondence
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Write standard form with zero placeholders, divide leading terms, multiply, subtract, repeat, and verify. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Divide polynomials using long and synthetic division and verify the division algorithm P=DQ+R.

manifests.title: P=DQ+R identity
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is omitting missing powers or distributing subtraction incorrectly. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Divide polynomials using long and synthetic division and verify the division algorithm P=DQ+R.

manifests.title: Remainder theorem substitution
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Is x+2 a factor of x^3-3x+2? Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Yes, because P(-2)=0.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use P(c) as the remainder on division by x-c and test whether x-c is a factor.

manifests.title: Factor-test loop
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Evaluate the candidate or use synthetic division, then divide confirmed factors out and continue. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use P(c) as the remainder on division by x-c and test whether x-c is a factor.

manifests.title: Multiplicity by repeated division
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is calling every rational candidate a factor before checking the remainder. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use P(c) as the remainder on division by x-c and test whether x-c is a factor.

manifests.title: Rational-root lattice
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Candidates for 2x^3+x^2-8x-4. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: ±1,±2,±4,±1/2.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Generate all possible rational zeros of an integer-coefficient polynomial and organize an efficient exact-and-numerical search.

manifests.title: Candidate workflow
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Let p divide the constant term and q divide the leading coefficient, reduce all signed ratios, and test candidates exactly. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Generate all possible rational zeros of an integer-coefficient polynomial and organize an efficient exact-and-numerical search.

manifests.title: Candidate versus root
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is treating the candidate list as the solution list or omitting fractional candidates. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Generate all possible rational zeros of an integer-coefficient polynomial and organize an efficient exact-and-numerical search.

manifests.title: Complex-root inventory
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Zeros 3±2i. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Real factor x^2-6x+13.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Count polynomial zeros over the complex numbers, use conjugate pairs for real coefficients, and build real polynomials from complex roots.

manifests.title: Conjugate reflection
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: For real coefficients, add conjugate roots, form real quadratic factors, and count all root slots. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Count polynomial zeros over the complex numbers, use conjugate pairs for real coefficients, and build real polynomials from complex roots.

manifests.title: Conjugate factor multiplication
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is allowing one isolated nonreal root in a real-coefficient polynomial. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Count polynomial zeros over the complex numbers, use conjugate pairs for real coefficients, and build real polynomials from complex roots.

manifests.title: Condition-to-factor builder
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Zeros -1 and 2 double, P(0)=8. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: P=2(x+1)(x-2)^2.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct polynomial functions from conditions, fit vertical scale, and approximate roots that lack convenient exact forms.

manifests.title: Numerical root refinement
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Write a product a∏(x-r)^m, use end behavior for degree and sign, solve a from a point, and approximate any remaining roots with justified numerical evidence. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct polynomial functions from conditions, fit vertical scale, and approximate roots that lack convenient exact forms.
